c.tagline: Lermontov's Caucasus spa town of mineral springs and mountain air.

taxi.fareNote: Yandex Go is by far the cheapest and most reliable option; street-hailed taxis are unmetered, so agree a price before getting in. Note that most foreign bank cards no longer work in Russia—carry cash.

emergency.note: 112 is the unified emergency number; 102 police, 103 ambulance, 101 fire.

avoid.reason: No no-go districts in town itself, though onward travel toward some neighboring North Caucasus areas warrants checking current advisories.

hood_desc: The elegant spa core at the foot of Mount Mashuk, centred on the Tsvetnik flower garden, the Lermontov Gallery, the Aeolian Harp, Diana's Grotto, and the historic mineral-water pump rooms; the classic first-timer base for 'taking the waters'.

The city's lively main avenue, lined with shops, cafes, restaurants, theatres, and 19th-century architecture; the most central and convenient place to stay, walkable to both the resort park and the markets.

The wooded slopes and sanatorium belt below Mashuk, reached by cable car, with the eerie blue Proval underground lake, health spas, and panoramic views toward Mount Elbrus; a calm nature-and-wellness setting.

The original hot-springs settlement on the south side, a traditional, largely residential district with a big Cossack market and local mineral baths; an authentic, budget-friendly, less touristy feel.
A quiet residential area around Novopyatigorsk Lake with a sandy swimming beach and parks; relaxed and family-friendly, away from the resort bustle.

water.note: Quality varies; most visitors drink bottled water or the town's famed mineral-spring water.

transit.hours: Trams and marshrutkas run roughly 5:30 AM to 11:00 PM; service thins out late evening.
transit.note: Pyatigorsk has one of Russia's narrow-gauge tram networks plus city buses and marshrutka (shared minibus) routes; Yandex Go fills the late-night gap.
transit.pay: Pay the driver or conductor in cash on board (a flat fare per ride); contactless bank cards work on many trams and marshrutkas. There is no separate tourist card.

bus: Intercity coaches from Pyatigorsk Bus Station
train: Suburban elektrichka to Mineralnye Vody and Kislovodsk

tip.r: Rounding up or leaving about 10% at sit-down restaurants is appreciated but not required.
